The L Component

Models for Immature Mosquito Ecology

Source: vignettes/L-interface.Rmd
L-interface.Rmd

The L component models aquatic mosquito ecology across larval habitats. This vignette describes its interfaces and the methods implemented by an L module.

The L component is linked to adult mosquito ecology through egg laying and emergence. F_eggs returns the number of eggs laid by adult mosquitoes in each patch, denoted by \(G\). The egg-laying interface distributes those eggs among habitats to produce the habitat-specific input \(\eta\). The L module then computes its dynamics and the emergence rate \(\alpha\) in each habitat. The emergence interface aggregates \(\alpha\), using the habitat membership matrix, into the patch-specific adult emergence rate \(\Lambda\).

The two interfaces are illustrated below.

Figure 1 - A diagram of the L Component in context

Module methods

Methods dispatch on the class of xds_obj$L_obj[[s]], where s is the vector-species index. Model-specific methods use s consistently. There is no fixed number of methods that every module must implement: implement the dynamics method that matches the model and the outputs and setup methods needed by its interfaces.

Dynamics

Implement one of the following:

  • dLdt.Lname for a continuous-time model. It receives t, the dependent-variable vector y, xds_obj, and s, and returns derivatives in the same order as the model’s state variables.
  • Update_Lt.Lname for a discrete-time model. It receives the same arguments and returns the updated state variables in state-variable order.

The functions are used by the continuous-time or discrete-time solver pathways, respectively.

Bionomics

LBionomics.Lname evaluates baseline bionomic parameter values at time t and resets their effect sizes. LEffectSizes.Lname applies vector-control effect sizes to those baseline values. Both methods receive t, y, xds_obj, and s, and return the updated xds_obj.

Egg input and emergence output

The egg-laying interface computes patch-level adult egg production \(G\) using F_eggs, then distributes eggs to aquatic habitats. If \(O\) is the habitat-by-patch egg-laying matrix, \(Q\) is the availability of modeled habitats in each patch, and \(Q_{\mathrm{all}}\) is total egg-laying availability, the habitat-level input is

\[ \eta = O\left(G \circ \frac{Q}{Q_{\mathrm{all}}}\right), \]

where \(\circ\) denotes element-wise multiplication. Thus, \(\eta\) has one value per habitat and is supplied to the L dynamics.

F_emerge.Lname returns the adult emergence quantity \(\alpha\), with one value per habitat. It is a rate for a continuous-time model and a number for a discrete-time model. The emergence interface aggregates habitat emergence by patch using the habitat membership matrix \(N\):

\[ \Lambda = N\alpha. \]

Model object, parameters, and state variables

make_L_obj_Lname creates the module-specific L object, and setup_L_obj.Lname attaches it to the full model at xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]. The setup method also receives the habitat-to-patch membership vector and initializes shared habitat interfaces.

  • get_L_pars.Lname returns the module’s parameters.
  • change_L_pars.Lname changes supported parameter values using the named list options.
  • setup_L_ix.Lname assigns indices to the module’s state variables; get_L_ix retrieves the stored indices.
  • get_L_vars.Lname extracts named states from y.
  • parse_L_orbits.Lname extracts named states and any model-specific derived quantities from the solver output matrix.

The number of state values is generally based on nHabitats, not nPatches. The membership vector associates each habitat with a patch.

Initial values and checks

make_L_inits_Lname returns a named list of default initial values for all state variables. setup_L_inits.Lname stores the values at xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]$inits; get_L_inits and change_L_inits.Lname inspect and update them.

setup_skillset_L.Lname records the module’s capabilities and limitations. check_L.Lname performs any module-specific consistency checks required before solving.

The basicL example

The basicL module tracks larval density \(L\) in each aquatic habitat. It uses the habitat-level egg input \(\eta\), maturation rate \(\psi\), crowding-dependent maturation parameter \(\xi\), density-independent mortality rate \(\phi\), and density-dependent mortality parameter \(\theta\). Its continuous-time equation is

\[ \frac{dL}{dt} = \eta - \left(\psi e^{-\xi L} + \phi + \theta L\right)L. \]

The corresponding habitat-level adult emergence rate is

\[ \alpha = \psi e^{-\xi L}L. \]

Setting \(\xi=0\) recovers the model described by Smith et al. (2013). basicL also implements Update_Lt.basicL and a numerical steady-state method, steady_state_L.basicL_ode.

Solving and visualization

steady_state_L.Lname is an optional method for computing a model’s steady state from habitat-level egg input \(\eta\). get_L_orbits retrieves the parsed L output from a solved xds object. The shared xds_plot_L and xds_lines_L functions plot aquatic mosquito population density; modules do not need to implement L-specific plotting generics.

For details on a specific model, see its module documentation and the relevant literature. The basicL equations are based on:

Smith DL, Perkins TA, Tusting LS, Scott TW, Lindsay SW (2013) Mosquito Population Regulation and Larval Source Management in Heterogeneous Environments. PLOS ONE 8(8): e71247. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0071247.
